liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Cold Rain & Snow** (2 reviews, 1 other source): Phil, wearing a huge novelty cowboy hat, stepped to a microphone in the encore and added end harmony vocals; Reviewer remarks on Phil singing on Cold Rain and Snow [6][17][24]
- **China Doll** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer singles out China Doll as awesome, and notes early Lesh singing; A rhythm section jam emerges from China Doll [1][23]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): Reviewer calls the opening song killer [20]
- **They Love Each Other** (1 review): Reviewer praises Jerry's solo as precise, note for note [20]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): China Cat into Rider ran at a quick pace because it was pouring and the band had no cover [28]
- **Drums** (1 review): Mickey's birthday drum solo coincided with the rainbow growing more intense behind the stage [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-09-10.139020.FOB.Beyer.billydee.Sellars.Noel.t.flac24** (recommended): source not stated; 22 songs; 169 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1983-09-10.162895.nak300-cp4.shields-hughes.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 153 min [3]. Said about its sound: Very clean recording with strong vocals, thick bold bass and good channel separation; set one has bass saturation in Brother Esau [3]
- **gd1983-09-10.nak300.deadjohn-or-bonner.96920.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 147 min [4]. Said about its sound: Uploader finds superior bass response and Phil bomb handling, preferring it to every circulating version, including the 24/96 MOTB transfer [4]
- **gd1983-09-10.fob.nak700.wagner.motb-0079.94508.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 143 min; rated 4.83/5 by 6 [7]
- **gd83-09-10.sennheiser.clugston.4860.shnf**: source not stated; 20 songs; 141 min; rated 4.54/5 by 13 [15]. Said about its sound: Described as a decent, warm audience recording, though not top notch, conveying the outdoor energy of crowd and band [20]

## Around the show

- Rain passed during the set break; in the second set a rainbow appeared behind the band as the sun set behind the audience [18]
- Reviewer, studying computers in Albuquerque, had only seen the Dead indoors before; this outdoor show revived his enthusiasm for Dead shows [19]
- Reviewer attended both nights, received a tarot death card in the campground, and passed out at the start of The Other One [21]
- Reviewer mentions green chiles and calls this the great second night of the run [23]
- Reviewer drove from Boulder for the shows; notes outdoor September shows in New Mexico and after-show antics in Santa Fe [24]
- Venue had a fort-style perimeter fence and roses attached to nearly every surface; tickets cost $13 [26]
- Wavy greeted arrivals at the desert camp entrance and directed them to quiet and noisy camping sides [26]
- The break was long; the band returned when rain stopped, with plastic over stage equipment, and fans danced in mud during set two [28]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-09-10.139020.FOB.Beyer.billydee.Sellars.Noel.t.flac24**: taped by billydee; transferred by Larry Sellers & the Philly Crew; Joe Noel; source: billydee recording (patched out of): Beyerdynamics 180's > Sony TC-D5M > master audio cassette (FOB); Larry Sellers & the Philly Crew Direct Stream Digital… [1]. Also: Tape pauses were smoothed with crossfades; filler used at the end of billydee's set one cassette [1]
- **gd1983-09-10.162895.nak300-cp4.shields-hughes.flac2496**: taped by Recording by Les Shields (Recording Guru) and Kevin T. Hughes, AICP, CEP (San Luis Obispo, CA 1981-1985).; transferred by Transfer and mastering by Kevin T. Hughes; source: FOB location – Master Audience Recording produced by a pair of Nak CM300 Microphones w/ CP4 Shotgun Caps > Sony D5 > Sony D6 Recorders > (Master) Maxell MX 90… [3]. Also: Taper used a Nak 300 on an 8-foot mic stand, 12 feet left of center from Healy's board [3]
- **gd1983-09-10.nak300.deadjohn-or-bonner.96920.flac16**: taped by Dead John or Bonner; source: Nak 300 > Nak 550 > MAC [4]. Also: Fresh transfer of master tapes recorded on a well-maintained Nak 550, in 16-bit/44.1kHz [4]
- **gd1983-09-10.fob.nak700.wagner.motb-0079.94508.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Adam Egert; source: (FOB) 2 x Nakamichi CM700 => Sony TC-D5m >> MAC [7]. Also: Quoting Bob Wagner: patched tape from Jaime Poris/Jim Olness rig, two or three Nak 700 omni capsules with foam for directionality; Reviewer recorded the show with a small handheld Sony recorder held at arm's length [25][28]
- **gd83-09-10.sennheiser.clugston.4860.shnf**: source: Sennheiser 441 mics > Technics SV100 PCM> DAT> CDR [15]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Dave's Picks Vol. 52: The Downs at Santa Fe, Santa Fe, NM (9/11/83)](https://store.dead.net/products/daves-picks-vol-52-the-downs-at-santa-fe-santa-fe-nm-9-11-83?variant=42469430067242) [31]
- Poster by Dennis Larkins: [Grateful Dead Santa Fe Downs NM 1983 D. Larkins Concert Poster](https://concertposterauction.com/Listing/Details/380816/Grateful-Dead-Santa-Fe-Downs-NM-1983-D-Larkins-Concert-Poster) [35]
- Poster by Dennis Larkins: [Grateful Dead Santa Fe Downs NM 1983 Hand-Colored D. Larkins Concert Poster](https://concertposterauction.com/Listing/Details/1210624/Grateful-Dead-Santa-Fe-Downs-NM-1983-HandColored-D-Larkins-Concert-Poster) [36]

claims.text: Phil, wearing a huge novelty cowboy hat, stepped to a microphone in the encore and added end harmony vocals
Rain passed during the set break; in the second set a rainbow appeared behind the band as the sun set behind the audience
Mickey's birthday drum solo coincided with the rainbow growing more intense behind the stage
Reviewer, studying computers in Albuquerque, had only seen the Dead indoors before; this outdoor show revived his enthusiasm for Dead shows
Reviewer praises Jerry's solo as precise, note for note
Described as a decent, warm audience recording, though not top notch, conveying the outdoor energy of crowd and band
Reviewer calls the opening song killer
Reviewer attended both nights, received a tarot death card in the campground, and passed out at the start of The Other One
Reviewer singles out China Doll as awesome, and notes early Lesh singing
Reviewer mentions green chiles and calls this the great second night of the run
Reviewer remarks on Phil singing on Cold Rain and Snow
Reviewer drove from Boulder for the shows; notes outdoor September shows in New Mexico and after-show antics in Santa Fe
Quoting Bob Wagner: patched tape from Jaime Poris/Jim Olness rig, two or three Nak 700 omni capsules with foam for directionality
Venue had a fort-style perimeter fence and roses attached to nearly every surface; tickets cost $13
Wavy greeted arrivals at the desert camp entrance and directed them to quiet and noisy camping sides
China Cat into Rider ran at a quick pace because it was pouring and the band had no cover
The break was long; the band returned when rain stopped, with plastic over stage equipment, and fans danced in mud during set two
Reviewer recorded the show with a small handheld Sony recorder held at arm's length
It rained during the show, though luckily no fish fell
A rhythm section jam emerges from China Doll
Tape pauses were smoothed with crossfades; filler used at the end of billydee's set one cassette
Taper used a Nak 300 on an 8-foot mic stand, 12 feet left of center from Healy's board
Very clean recording with strong vocals, thick bold bass and good channel separation; set one has bass saturation in Brother Esau
Fresh transfer of master tapes recorded on a well-maintained Nak 550, in 16-bit/44.1kHz
Uploader finds superior bass response and Phil bomb handling, preferring it to every circulating version, including the 24/96 MOTB transfer
Uploader says this was the only time Cold Rain and Snow served as an encore
